cells: import polars as pl from great_tables import GT, loc, md, style import gt_extras as gte nfl_df = pl.read_json("../data/gt-extras/nfl_2011_stats.json") def make_gt(df) -> GT: return ( GT(df, rowname_col="Team", groupname_col="team_division") .tab_header( title="2011 NFL Season at a Glance", subtitle="Super Bowl XLVI: New York Giants def. New England Patriots", ) .tab_source_note( md( 'Source: [Lee Sharpe, nflverse](https://github.com/nflverse/nfldata)' ) ) .tab_stubhead(label="Team") .tab_spanner(label="Scoring", columns=["Avg PF", "Avg PA", "Point Diff"]) .tab_spanner(label="Season Trends", columns=["Games", "Streak"]) .fmt_number(columns="Point Diff", decimals=1) .fmt_image("team_logo_espn") .cols_hide(["Wins", "team_conf", "team_name"]) .cols_align(align="center", columns=["Avg PF", "Avg PA", "Games"]) # Great Tables 1.1 moves no column after the stub: the logo goes first .cols_move_to_start("team_logo_espn") .cols_label({"team_logo_espn": ""}) .pipe( gte.gt_plt_winloss, column="Games", win_color="blue", loss_color="orange", tie_color="gray", height=40, width=120, ) .pipe( gte.gt_fa_rank_change, column="Streak", icon_type="turn", color_up="blue", color_down="orange", size=14, ) .pipe( gte.gt_plt_dumbbell, col1="Avg PF", col2="Avg PA", col1_color="green", col2_color="red", width=300, height=40, num_decimals=0, label="Points For vs Points Against", font_size=12, ) .pipe( gte.gt_color_box, columns="Point Diff", palette=["green", "yellow", "red"], domain=[14, -14] ) # Great Tables 1.1 styles the stub only through loc.stub(), not as a column .tab_style(style.fill(color="lightgray"), loc.stub()) .pipe(gte.gt_highlight_rows, rows="NYG", fill="gold", alpha=0.3) .pipe(gte.gt_highlight_rows, rows="NE", fill="silver", alpha=0.3) .pipe(gte.gt_add_divider, columns="Point Diff", color="darkblue", weight=3) .pipe(gte.gt_theme_538) ) gt1 = make_gt(nfl_df.head(16)) gt2 = make_gt(nfl_df.slice(16, 16)) gte.gt_two_column_layout(gt1, gt2, table_header_from=1)
